title: Backend Engineer - Payments Platform - 2025
content: Role: Backend Engineer, Payments Platform. Summary: Northstar Digital is seeking a backend engineer to build secure, observable services for payment processing and merchant operations. Responsibilities: design and maintain REST APIs; implement asynchronous workflows; review code; improve test coverage; investigate production issues; document service contracts; and collaborate with product, QA, security, and frontend engineers. Required skills: Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, REST API design, SQL, Git, automated testing with Pytest, and practical Docker experience. Preferred skills: Redis, RabbitMQ or Kafka, AWS, CI/CD pipelines, OpenTelemetry, and experience with payment systems. Qualifications: bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience. Experience: minimum 3 years of professional backend software development. Selection criteria: evidence of maintainable Python code, API and database design ability, secure coding awareness, debugging approach, written communication, and collaboration. Interview process: recruiter screen, 60-minute Python coding exercise, 60-minute system-design interview, and behavioral interview. The coding exercise must be relevant to normal backend work and may not request production company data.

title: Senior Backend Engineer - Core Services - 2024
content: Role: Senior Backend Engineer, Core Services. Summary: Lead the design and delivery of reliable services used by Northstar Digital products. Responsibilities: own service architecture; turn product requirements into technical plans; mentor engineers; lead reviews; define observability and reliability standards; plan safe migrations; and participate in an on-call rotation. Required skills: at least 5 years of backend development, advanced Python, FastAPI or Django, PostgreSQL, distributed-systems fundamentals, API security, Docker, CI/CD, and production troubleshooting. Preferred skills: Kubernetes, AWS, Terraform, event-driven architecture, Kafka, Redis, and technical leadership. Qualifications: bachelor's degree in a computing discipline or equivalent demonstrable engineering experience. Selection criteria: architecture judgment, ability to explain trade-offs, operational ownership, code quality, mentoring ability, and inclusive collaboration. Interview process: experience review, practical code-review exercise, distributed-system design interview, leadership interview, and values interview.

title: Frontend Engineer - Customer Experience - 2025
content: Role: Frontend Engineer, Customer Experience. Summary: Build accessible and responsive web experiences for customer and operations teams. Responsibilities: deliver React features; translate designs into reusable components; integrate REST APIs; write automated tests; monitor frontend performance; and work closely with design, backend, and QA. Required skills: TypeScript, React, semantic HTML, modern CSS, state management, API integration, Git, and frontend testing. Preferred skills: Vite, Tailwind CSS, Playwright, design systems, web performance, and accessibility auditing. Qualifications: bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field, a relevant diploma, or equivalent portfolio and professional experience. Experience: minimum 2 years building production web applications. Selection criteria: component design, accessibility, testing discipline, problem solving, user empathy, and communication. Interview process: portfolio discussion, practical React exercise, frontend architecture interview, and behavioral interview.

title: Machine Learning Engineer - Talent Intelligence - 2025
content: Role: Machine Learning Engineer, Talent Intelligence. Summary: Develop and evaluate responsible NLP and retrieval systems for recruitment workflows. Responsibilities: prepare governed datasets; train and evaluate models; implement retrieval pipelines; expose models through APIs; monitor quality and drift; document experiments; and partner with product, engineering, and compliance. Required skills: Python, machine learning fundamentals, NLP, information retrieval, data validation, SQL, experiment tracking, and API development. Preferred skills: PyTorch, Hugging Face, vector databases, RAG evaluation, FastAPI, Docker, and cloud deployment. Qualifications: bachelor's or master's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, or a related discipline, or equivalent applied experience. Experience: minimum 3 years in software or machine-learning engineering, including at least 1 year deploying ML systems. Selection criteria: experimental rigor, evaluation design, production engineering, responsible-AI awareness, communication, and collaboration. Interview process: project deep dive, Python and data exercise, ML-system design interview, responsible-AI scenario, and behavioral interview.

title: Northstar Digital Engineering Hiring Policy - 2025
content: Purpose: provide a consistent, fair, and evidence-based process for engineering hiring at the fictional company Northstar Digital. Every job description must distinguish required skills from preferred skills and must state responsibilities, qualification alternatives, experience expectations, and selection criteria. Equivalent professional experience must be considered when a degree is not legally or operationally necessary. Requirements must be demonstrably related to the role. Interview panels must use the same published criteria for every candidate in the same hiring round. At least two trained reviewers must contribute to the final decision. Reviewers must record job-related evidence and must not use protected characteristics, photographs, age assumptions, family status, disability, religion, gender, ethnicity, or other non-job-related information. Candidate data must be accessed only for recruitment, stored in approved systems, and retained according to the applicable retention schedule. AI-generated recommendations are decision support only; a human interviewer remains accountable for shortlisting and final decisions. Reasonable accommodations must be offered throughout the selection process.

title: Northstar Digital Engineering Interview Rubric - 2025
content: Engineering candidates are assessed using five evidence categories. Technical fundamentals: demonstrates accurate knowledge of the languages, frameworks, data stores, and engineering practices required by the role. Problem solving: clarifies assumptions, decomposes problems, evaluates trade-offs, and validates the solution. Quality and reliability: considers testing, security, observability, failure handling, maintainability, and operational impact. Communication and collaboration: explains decisions clearly, listens, incorporates feedback, and works constructively across disciplines. Learning and ownership: identifies gaps honestly, learns from incidents, follows through, and improves systems. Each category is rated from 1 to 4 using written behavioral anchors. A rating must include interview evidence; intuition-only ratings are not acceptable. Required-skill gaps must be recorded separately from preferred-skill gaps. A candidate is not rejected solely for lacking a preferred skill. For backend roles, the standard assessment normally includes a role-relevant coding exercise and a system-design discussion.
